summary: preinstall hook fetches Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundled payload at install time
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, string-array indirection) and at install time downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the platform-specific bun binary to a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it via execFileSync to run the sibling math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript bundle (rotated string array, hex-encoded identifiers) whose contents bear no relation to the package's advertised chat-UI purpose. The package presents itself as a React/MobX chat UI component library, so pulling in a second language runtime and executing an obfuscated bundle under it at npm install time is inconsistent with the declared purpose. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: an official-runtime fetch is used as the execution vehicle for a bundled opaque payload that is fetched-or-shipped-but-obfuscated and executed automatically on install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
